channel.title: Farmer's Weekly SA - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Farmer's Weekly SA (farmersweekly.co.za)

item.title: Steenhuisen addresses concerns over Foot-and-mouth disease crisis
item.description: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) continues to spread beyond its epicentre in KwaZulu-Natal, the Free State and North West and Agriculture Minister John Steenhuisen admits the outbreak remains a serious concern.

item.title: Small is beautiful for budding Overberg trout business
item.description: Albert Kemp has turned a childhood fascination with fish into a sophisticated, year-round aquaculture enterprise on a smallholding owned by himself and his wife Alicia in Baardskeerdersbos near Gansbaai.

item.title: Steenhuisen: ‘FMD is not under control but we have a plan to break its back’
item.description: South Africa’s escalating foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreak is “certainly not under control”, Minister of Agriculture John Steenhuisen told Farmer’s Weekly in an interview on Thursday, but he insists a decisive vaccination strategy, tighter biosecurity, and stronger public-private coordination will turn the tide.

item.title: Canning industry faces mounting pressure from climate, markets, tariffs
item.description: The South African canning industry is navigating a tough season as dry, warm climatic conditions, tight markets, and a stronger rand collide with ongoing uncertainty around US tariffs.

item.title: Eastern Cape agricultural show in Gqeberha celebrates smallholder success
item.description: The Eastern Cape Department of Agriculture hosted its fourth agricultural show on 17 February in Gqeberha, uniting farmers from the Nelson Mandela Bay Metro and Sarah Baartman District Municipalities.

item.title: Toyota gears up for SA rollout of all-new RAV4
item.description: The latest generation of the world’s best-selling car model of 2024, the Toyota RAV4, is heading to South Africa this year. The Citizen’s Charl Bosch reports.

item.title: Three reasons for hope in the wake of FMD crisis
item.description: As foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) continues to wreak havoc on South African livestock farms, disrupting auctions, halting exports and placing enormous financial strain on producers, three significant developments this week are offering a measure of hope to an embattled industry.

item.title: Self-driving sprayers: cost-effective amid rising compliance pressure
item.description: Farmer’s Weekly recently had an opportunity to witness the compact, self-driving OSAM S500 PRO Multi-function Sprayer in action in a table grape vineyard in the Hex River Valley, Western Cape.

item.title: Macadamia industry at export crossroads with hard lessons ahead
item.description: South Africa’s macadamia industry is at a turning point. After a decade of rapid growth and high prices, the sector is now entering a period of consolidation, tighter margins and increased structural risk, particularly concerning the growing export of unshelled nuts to Asia.

item.title: Strong rand puts damper on bigger citrus crop
item.description: The growing citrus crop is expected to put pressure on South African farmers this year as existing export markets near saturation. Compounding the effect is a stronger exchange rate, which is set to erode margins.
